newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Burundi opposition urges military action in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: Burundi opposition urges military action in Zaire.

text.p: Burundi's Hutu-dominated opposition party, Frodebu, called on Wednesday for international military action to protect refugees fleeing from fighting in eastern Zaire.
"Frodebu continues to seek international military intervention to protect Hutu refugees in the region and to guarantee humanitarian aid," the party said in a statement released in Brussels.

Frodebu pinned the blame for the crisis in Zaire's Kivu region firmly on Rwanda and Burundi's Tutsi-led armies acting "under the cover" of a rebellion by Zaire's ethnic Tutsis, the Banyamulenge, and other un-named Zairean opposition groups.

Burundi's military regime came to power on July 25 in an coup that brought ethnic Tutsi Pierre Buyoya to power. Regional states including Tanzania, Kenya and Zaire imposed sanctions on Burundi six days later.
Frodebu said these sanctions should now be toughened.
The statement was released ahead of a news conference by Frodebu leader Jean Minani in Brussels on Thursday.
Earlier on Wednesday, Burundi's Tutsi-dominated army denied killing dozens of suspected Hutu rebels who disappeared at a border crossing with war-torn east Zaire.

Refugees, aid workers, diplomats and human rights officials say the army has screened thousands of Hutu refugees forced home to Burundi from east Zaire since fighting erupted two weeks ago, and dozens of people have not been seen since.
They presume they were killed, as dozens of bodies of men, women and children are washing up on the shores of Lake Tanganyika at the south end of the border between Zaire and Burundi.
